name: Polaris
astronomy: Polaris is a multiple-star system near Earth's north celestial pole, so it appears nearly fixed in the northern sky.
symbolism: Across many northern traditions, its steady apparent position has made it a cultural symbol of orientation and constancy.

name: Vega
astronomy: Vega is a bright A-type main-sequence star in Lyra, about 25 light-years from Earth.
symbolism: In the Chinese Qixi story it is associated with the Weaver Girl, a cultural image of craft, distance, and reunion.

name: Sirius
astronomy: Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky and a nearby binary system in Canis Major.
symbolism: Its striking brightness has been used as a seasonal marker in several cultures and can evoke alertness and brilliance.

name: Rigel
astronomy: Rigel is a luminous blue supergiant in Orion, roughly 860 light-years away.
symbolism: As a prominent point in Orion's figure, it is often linked in sky lore with scale, presence, and the vastness of winter skies.

name: Betelgeuse
astronomy: Betelgeuse is a red supergiant in Orion whose brightness varies noticeably over time.
symbolism: Its warm color and changing light provide a cultural image of transformation and visible change.

name: Altair
astronomy: Altair is a rapidly rotating A-type star about 17 light-years away in Aquila.
symbolism: Chinese sky lore pairs Altair with the Cowherd, a symbol in a traditional story about connection across the Milky Way.

name: Arcturus
astronomy: Arcturus is an orange giant and the brightest star in Boötes, about 37 light-years away.
symbolism: Easy to find by following the Big Dipper's handle, it can symbolize a path revealed through patient observation.

name: Antares
astronomy: Antares is a red supergiant in Scorpius, visually comparable in color to Mars.
symbolism: Its red light has inspired names related to rivals and hearts, giving it a traditional association with intensity and contrast.

name: Capella
astronomy: Capella is a bright system of four stars in Auriga, dominated visually by two giant stars.
symbolism: Its winter prominence has made it a useful seasonal beacon, a cultural motif of return and recurring cycles.

name: Aldebaran
astronomy: Aldebaran is an orange giant that appears among the Hyades in Taurus but is much closer to Earth.
symbolism: Its eye-like position in Taurus has made it a vivid figure in traditional sky stories and a symbol of watchfulness.

name: Pleiades
astronomy: The Pleiades are a young open star cluster about 444 light-years away in Taurus.
symbolism: The compact cluster appears in seasonal traditions around the world and can symbolize gathering, shared memory, and many lights together.

name: Orion Nebula
astronomy: The Orion Nebula is a nearby stellar nursery in Orion where gas and dust form new stars.
symbolism: As a visible region of stellar birth, it offers a cultural image of emergence, making, and unfinished possibility.

name: Andromeda Galaxy
astronomy: Andromeda is the nearest large galaxy to the Milky Way, about 2.5 million light-years away.
symbolism: Its faint, distant glow can symbolize perspective: a reminder that familiar skies contain immense depth.

name: Mizar and Alcor
astronomy: Mizar and Alcor are a well-known naked-eye double in the Big Dipper; Mizar itself is a multiple-star system.
symbolism: Because two points can be seen together with careful viewing, this pair is a cultural image of companionship and attention.

name: Deneb
astronomy: Deneb is a very luminous blue-white supergiant in Cygnus and one corner of the Summer Triangle.
symbolism: Its place in a prominent asterism has made it a traditional marker for tracing patterns and connections across the night sky.
